facts_found: EcoCard earns 5 sustainability points per dollar on qualifying Green purchases and 1 point per dollar on other purchases. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_002]

EcoCard Green category generally includes public transportation, EV charging, renewable energy subscriptions, certified sustainable retailers/eco-labeled products, and bike share/micromobility. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_003]

EcoCard merchants Target, Walmart, Amazon, and ThredUp do NOT earn the 5 points/$ rate; they earn the standard 1 point/$ (applies to all channels, including eco-labeled items and Amazon-marketplace orders processed by Amazon). [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_004]
EcoCard EV charging qualifies for the higher 5 points/$ rate only on Tesla Supercharger, ChargePoint, or EVgo; all other charging networks earn the standard 1 point/$. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_004]
On EcoCard, gift cards and cash equivalents typically do not qualify as Green purchases; mixed carts at non-partner merchants may earn only the non-Green rate. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_003]

Business Bronze Rewards Card earns 1.0% cash back on eligible purchases, calculated on the net transaction amount after credits or returns; there are no bonus category multipliers. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_bronze_rewards_card_002]

Business Bronze Rewards Card merchants earning 0% cash back: WeWork, Regus, Industrious (coworking) and Gusto, ADP, Paychex, Rippling (payroll processors). [doc_business_credit_cards_business_bronze_rewards_card_003]

Business Bronze Rewards Card SaaS merchants Slack, Zoom, HubSpot, and Salesforce earn 1.0% only for the first 12 months of the subscription; auto-renewals/continued payments after 12 months earn 0%. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_bronze_rewards_card_003]

All credit card rewards are stored as 'points' regardless of card type; for cash-back cards including Business Bronze Rewards Card, 1 point = $0.01 when redeemed as statement/checking credit. EcoCard is the only true points-based card (sustainability points), also redeeming at $0.01 per point. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_006]

Rounding policy: all credit card rewards points are rounded DOWN (floored/truncated) to the nearest whole number per transaction; fractional points are never rounded up. This applies across all card types and categories. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007]

Valid rewards transaction categories used by Rho-Bank are: Travel, Software, Media, Green, Sustainable, Operations, Transportation, Groceries, Dining, Entertainment, Utilities, Shopping, Other (Other = card-specific exclusions/exceptions). [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_005]
Returns/refunds/chargebacks reverse previously earned rewards at the original earn rate; disputed transactions do not earn rewards until resolved and posted. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_002]
For EcoCard, balance transfers, cash equivalents, and fees do not count toward the new-customer promo spending threshold (offer window 2025-08-01 to 2025-12-15). [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_009]
No earning cap (monthly/annual maximum rewards) was documented for either the EcoCard or the Business Bronze Rewards Card. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_bronze_rewards_card_002]
When correcting rewards, the new value must be expressed as a whole-number point count (floored), not a dollar amount or decimal. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004]

open_questions: No KB document explicitly states whether EcoCard cash advances, balance transfers, fees, or interest earn 0 points on the base 1 point/$ rate (the 0%/exclusion language was found only in the new-customer promo threshold context and in other cards' terms).
No KB document confirms a rewards earning cap for either card; absence of a cap document was treated as 'no documented cap' rather than an explicit 'no cap' statement.

The exact merchant-category-code mapping that determines whether a given October-November 2025 transaction is 'Green' vs 'Other' on the EcoCard is not enumerated in the KB (only example merchant types and named exclusions are provided).
Whether the Business Bronze first-12-month SaaS clock is measured from subscription start or account opening is not specified in the exclusion document.

facts_found: No user-callable tool is documented for the EcoCard in-app merchant directory; the KB describes eligibility checking as a manual in-app action (open the directory, filter for certified green partners, look for the green badge on merchant profiles and at checkout). [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_007]

The in-app merchant directory is presented as a customer-facing feature with a filter and a 'feedback option' to suggest missing merchants, not as a tool with a signature or arguments; no tool name/parameters for a merchant-eligibility lookup appear anywhere in the KB. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_007]

The only user-performable tool documented in the EcoCard rewards flow is submit_cash_back_dispute_0589(user_id, transaction_id), used after a purchase to dispute a cash-back/earn-rate discrepancy, not to verify merchant eligibility before purchase. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_003]

A transaction category of 'Green' is not authoritative for the 5x rate: 5 points/$ applies only at qualifying green merchants and categories, and the named exclusions (Target, Walmart, Amazon, ThredUp) earn the standard 1 point/$ even for eco-labeled/sustainable items. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_004]

Eligibility is determined by the merchant meeting green criteria / being a certified partner; the statement/receipt 'green indicator' is described only as something eligible transactions 'may display,' and the authoritative pre-purchase check is the green badge in the merchant directory. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_003]

Edge cases where a 'Green'-looking purchase may not qualify: marketplaces/delivery platforms processing through non-green parent entities, mixed carts at non-partner merchants lacking item-level green data, and gift cards/cash equivalents. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_003]
For EV charging specifically, only Tesla Supercharger, ChargePoint, and EVgo qualify for the 5x rate; all other charging networks earn 1x regardless of category. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_004]

If a customer believes a purchase should have qualified for the higher rate, the documented path is to contact support with the receipt and merchant details for review (and/or file a cash-back dispute), confirming that the recorded category alone does not settle eligibility. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_003]

facts_found: No KB document states an explicit review duration/SLA for a cash-back (rewards) dispute in SUBMITTED status; the flow is only described as queued for review. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_003]

When submitting a cash-back dispute, the customer is advised that supporting context (e.g., category or promotion expectations) may be requested later during review, but no notification channel or timeline is specified. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_003]

The customer-facing cash-back guidance directs customers to contact support (1-800-RHO-BANK, in-app chat, or rhobank.com/help) about a discrepancy; it states the correct amount will be applied if the customer was shortchanged but gives no defined notification method or review SLA. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_021]
The rewards adjustment does NOT post automatically after a cash-back dispute is approved; an agent must manually apply it. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004]

After a cash-back dispute is resolved and approved, the required steps are: look up the user's resolved disputes in the cash_back_disputes database to find transaction_id(s), unlock update_transaction_rewards_3847, independently recalculate rewards, then call update_transaction_rewards_3847 and confirm the update in credit_card_transaction_history. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004]
The dispute record's expected_rewards field must not be relied on; rates and eligibility are verified independently during the manual correction. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004]

Provisional-credit and debit/Reg E dispute timelines (e.g., 10/45/90 days, 'few days to several weeks') govern disputed transaction amounts, not cash-back rewards discrepancies, and should not be applied to a SUBMITTED cash-back dispute. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_022]

EcoCard Green category generally includes public transportation, EV charging, renewable energy subscriptions, certified sustainable retailers/eco-labeled products, and bike share/micromobility. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_003]

EcoCard merchants Target, Walmart, Amazon, and ThredUp do NOT earn the 5 points/$ rate; they earn the standard 1 point/$ (applies to all channels, including eco-labeled items and Amazon-marketplace orders processed by Amazon). [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_004]
EcoCard EV charging qualifies for the higher 5 points/$ rate only on Tesla Supercharger, ChargePoint, or EVgo; all other charging networks earn the standard 1 point/$. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_004]
On EcoCard, gift cards and cash equivalents typically do not qualify as Green purchases; mixed carts at non-partner merchants may earn only the non-Green rate. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_003]

Business Bronze Rewards Card earns 1.0% cash back on eligible purchases, calculated on the net transaction amount after credits or returns; there are no bonus category multipliers. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_bronze_rewards_card_002]
